column3: Definition 1 and its following satisfaction paragraph give the displayed switching repertoire and baseline quartet exclusion used in Lemma 1; the source uses these objects without a numbered citation.

Definition 2 supplies the original endpoint pair extracted below the selected edge, making the canonical T+e in the formal statement precise; this is endpoint data, not an alternative attribution theorem.

Supplementary representation bridge: the paper defines T+e by deletion and unary suppression, whereas its Lean realization is a canonical endpoint-pair graph. Proving the single-edge suppression bridge reuses Lemma 2 in ghostEndpoints_mem_unique to identify canonical wire endpoints. This is the same vertex-disjoint-cycle invariant; Observation 2 and the independent disjoint-cycle uniqueness argument remain the attribution proof.
Definition 3's actual edge-above graph represents T+e; deletion/suppression is proved equivalent to this canonical graph rather than assumed.
The main proof describes correctly precomputed single-edge quartet weights and sums them via Lemma 1, thereby using Eq. 1 without naming its equation number.
The proof searches for one edge maximizing s(y) and identifies its score with s(y), using Eq. 3's candidate maximum without a numbered citation.
The source proof optimizes satisfied quartets of switching trees and excludes the support-tree baseline; Definition 1 and its satisfaction paragraph define those objects without a proof citation.
The proof's cases use target nodes and assigned non-tree edges, the data of Procedure ASSIGN in Definition 2.
The proof outputs edges added above original endpoint pairs and a level-1 extension; Definition 3's edge-above operation is made into an actual graph construction.
Precomputed single-edge score contributions use Definition 4's delta multiplicity weights, which the source discusses immediately before the recurrence.
Eq. 4/5 and the child-subproblem proof use Definition 5's children in the actual network, including subdivided endpoints; the source uses this notation without a numbered citation.
